README: A whole-piece reading: every mark an edition prints for one fugue, in every voice and bar, attached to the game's own notes.

Notes are addressed as in data/touch/pieces.json: v = voice index (here 0 Soprano, 1 Alto, 2 Bass, pieces.json voiceNames), on = onset tick (tpq 1920; a 4/4 bar is 7680 ticks; bar n starts at (n-1)*7680). p (MIDI) and name are a check (names are the game's spelling, even where the edition renotates), bar and pos (sixteenths from the barline) are for people.

marks[]: one note's articulation. art is one of staccato (dot), wedge (Keil: shorter and sharper), tenuto (dash: full value, a slight lean), portato (dash over dot: held a little apart, each note weighted), accent (>), marcato (^ over a dot: struck hard and left), fermata. A note may have two marks (wedge+tenuto).

slurs[]: spans in one voice, from and to both included. kind "slur" = a group played as one gesture (joined inside, the last note lighter and, with lastShort, let go early); kind "portato" = dots under a slur (each note detached a little but carried in one line); kind "phrase" = a long phrasing arc over a whole subject or line. role says what the slur covers.
dyn[]: a printed level at a time, for the voices it was printed for (Busoni prints dynamics per staff, sometimes per voice).

hairpins[]: cresc/dim spans in time for the given voices. text[]: words printed in the score with an English gloss. tempo.changes[] is left empty on purpose: the owner has ruled out tempo warping except at fermatas, so Busoni's tempo words are kept only in tempo.notes[] (applied: false) and fermatas stay in marks[].

breaths[]: a printed caesura before a note. voicing[]: pianistic re-voicings, recorded as notes only and not to be applied: octave-doubling (interval in semitones) and added notes. ornaments[]: a printed ornament and how Busoni realises it.
rules[]: instructions that apply to unmarked notes; the game must apply these by rule. sections[]: Busoni's double bars.
fingering: a summary of patterns and a few samples (fingers in the order of the notes from that note on); not every digit is transcribed.
footnotes[]: German text (as printed, old spelling kept) and an English translation.
conf on every item: sure (clearly printed and placed), likely (printed, the placement or the sign read from a 300 dpi scan with some doubt), unsure (a guess: hard to see, or inferred).
This format is a superset of docs/wtc/readings/*.json: the old per-note subject marks can be derived from marks[] and slurs[] on the first entry.
title: Fugue 20 in A minor, BWV 889

edition.author: Ferruccio B. Busoni
edition.title: Johann Sebastian Bach, Das Wohltemperierte Klavier, Zweiter Teil, bearbeitet und erläutert von Ferruccio Busoni (Busoni-Ausgabe, Band II)

tempo.en: no tempo word printed; footnote NB (p.6): the 32nd figures shared with the prelude allow almost the same tempo for both

character: sempre forte; the subject tenuto ma non legato with wedged eighths, the 32nd countersubject "(trotzig)" (defiant), slurred run by run.
dynamicPlan: sempre forte throughout (b.1); small swells in b.9 and b.13; a crescendo to fz on the bass B♭ (b.21); no other levels.
